summary: Verified plan v1 of build northwind-sales (scale: project, build_mode: design-only, 4 milestones / 16 steps) on all three lenses. Executability passed 16/16. Grounding failed on M3-S02, M4-S01 and M4-S02. Testability failed on M2-S04 and M3-S04. Five blockers, ten warnings, thirteen cross-step checks of which one failed. All 19 declared checkers exist and run in their declared form, and every empty-directory and non-existent-directory claim the plan makes about them was reproduced by probe. One prose-only amendment was applied to M4-S03. Status set to plan-rejected; G2 is not offered.
confidence_rationale: All three lenses ran on every one of the 16 steps. Every verdict carries evidence naming the file read or the command run and its output. No refutation rests on a file being absent: PV-B02 rests on quoted text that contradicts the decision, PV-B04/PV-B05 on a reproducible regex scan of assumptions[].because, and PV-B01/PV-B03 on the declared acceptance_tests[] type lists themselves. build_plan.py validate ran before and after the write with identical output.

findings.title: M2-S04 refuted on the testability lens
findings.detail: [testability lens] Step type is `validation` — one of the seven metadata types — and acceptance_tests[] carries neither an `xml` test nor a `manifest` test. It declares artefacts/M2-S04/package.xml in outputs[] but nothing in the plan asserts the manifest or the XML parse.  FIX: Add an `xml` test and a `manifest` test, in the shape M2-S03 already uses. Practical impact is low — section 5 runs both checks always-on whether declared or not — but the step's declared test surface is what a reader of plan.json and PLAN.md sees, and at unblock time this one is incomplete.

findings.title: M3-S02 refuted on the grounding lens
findings.detail: [grounding lens] Decision D9 ships the approval process `active true` on the stated authority of admin/approval-process-apex-patterns gotcha 14, and records the two approval skills as contradicting each other on deploying inactive. Neither claim holds. Gotcha 14 is titled 'a null `processDefinitionNameOrId` routes by org process order, which deploys don't carry' and says nothing about a named process requiring State Active — its subject is the opposite case. And the skill D9 names as governing says, in its own words, the opposite of D9's conclusion: 'The approval process is deployed <active>true</active> here because it is a fixture. A production process should deploy inactive and be activated after its workflow actions and templates exist.' So the two skills do not disagree; both say deploy inactive for production.  FIX: Re-ground D9. The real tension is intra-skill — that skill's prose (deploy inactive) against its own checker rule at check_approval_process_apex_patterns.py:376-386 (HIGH on <active>false</active> while Apex in the tree names the process), and its actual support for the Active requirement is metadata-examples.md:49-52 ('an inactive process is invisible to a submission that names it') plus templates/approval-process-apex-patterns-template.md:30. Either (a) ship active false, move activation into the cutover runbook beside A34, and correct M3-S03's checker test `expected`, which the plan's own fixture proves exits 1 at active false; or (b) keep active true, cite the two sources that do support it, and record the overridden production guidance as an accepted risk carrying the process-order prerequisite.

findings.detail: [grounding lens] templates/apex/tests/TestDataFactory.cls-meta.xml pins <apiVersion>67.0</apiVersion> while the step declares api_version 62.0 for its four authored classes. Section 4's Apex row note requires the template to ship 'as a verbatim copy (with its meta XML)', so a verbatim ship puts a 67.0 class beside four 62.0 ones. The step's manual test pins only the .cls diff, so the mismatch is undetected.  FIX: Say in the step note which version the shipped meta XML carries, and extend the manual test to cover it. This also matters for the read idiom: AGENT_CONTRACT's Apex security table makes WITH USER_MODE correct at 62.0 and default user mode the 67.0 behaviour.

findings.title: M2-S04's skill-gap block is upheld, and the platform answer is known
findings.detail: The block is correct as a LIBRARY gap: grep -rn HasOpportunityLineItem skills/ templates/ standards/ returns exactly one hit (admin/pipeline-review-design/references/gotchas.md:91, report-column filterability, silent on formula context), and search_knowledge.py reproduces the planner's recorded result. No skill documents how a validation rule counts child rows. The platform answer is nonetheless known: Opportunity carries a standard read-only Boolean HasOpportunityLineItem, and the repo's own corpus states its semantics at knowledge/imports/salesforce-channel-revenue-management.md:4696 — 'The Opportunity HasOpportunityLineItem field is set to true when an OpportunityLineItem is inserted for that Opportunity.' A rule of the shape AND(ISPICKVAL(StageName,'Propose'), NOT(HasOpportunityLineItem)) is the standard mechanism. This verifier does not author that claim: the import establishes the field's existence and when it is set, not its availability in validation-rule formula context, and turning recall into a grounded claim is what the block exists to prevent. AMEND PATH: deepen skills/admin/validation-rules or skills/admin/products-and-pricebooks with the documented line-item-count mechanism and its official source, then `build_plan.py amend-step <plan> M2-S04 --file <inputs>` — M2-S04 is `blocked`, which amend-step's step-status precondition admits — adding the errorConditionFormula to inputs{} and the xml + manifest tests PV-B01 names, and `set-status M2-S04 pending`.

deliverables.title: Verification report — northwind-sales plan v1
deliverables.content: See the markdown twin at the same stem: verdict matrix, five blockers with evidence and remedy, ten warnings, thirteen cross-step results, the rejection line and the Process Observations.

process_observations.observation: Every one of the plan's stated checker behaviours was reproducible: 19 checkers, 33 declared commands, and every empty-directory and non-existent-directory claim matched the observed exit code and message.

evidence.detail: All 33 commands run verbatim from the build directory with the artefacts/ tree empty; plus a /nonexistent and an empty-directory probe per checker. No usage errors, no unrecognised flags.

process_observations.observation: The planner's three hardest structural calls are all correct in source, not merely plausible: the two-argument-surface approval commands, the non-recursive opportunity-management checker, and the Apex-exception manifest split.

evidence.detail: line 366 appends root_dir/'approvalProcesses' for --manifest-dir (non-recursive) while line 107 uses path.rglob for a positional path, so neither surface alone works; check_opportunity_management.py uses bp_dir.glob / rt_dir.glob / path_dir.glob (fixed paths, no rglob), so step scope is the only live scope; M3-S03 declares no package.xml and M3-S04 claims the depends_on-manifest clause rather than the Apex exception, which is apex-builder-only.

process_observations.observation: Every checker rule id the plan cites by name exists with the severity and threshold the plan states, across seven different checkers.

evidence.detail: CP-DESC-01 ERROR >255 / CP-DESC-02 INFO >200; PSA-DESC-01 ERROR >255 / PSA-DESC-02 INFO >200; RPT-COL-01 INFO; VR-PICK-01; IM001 CRITICAL; RL-REQ-03 ADVISORY — all confirmed at the cited severities.

process_observations.observation: admin/approval-process-apex-patterns contradicts itself: its prose says a production approval process should deploy inactive, while its own checker raises HIGH on exactly that when Apex in the tree names the process.

evidence.detail: line 515: 'A production process should deploy inactive and be activated after its workflow actions and templates exist' — against check_approval_process_apex_patterns.py:376-386, HIGH on <active>false</active> while Apex in this tree submits to the named process. A plan cannot satisfy both. This is a library defect the plan ran into, not one it created.

process_observations.observation: admin/path-and-guidance's FlexiPage sample omits the <identifier> element that has been required since API 53.0 and that the record-page checker raises as an ERROR.

evidence.detail: section 4, lines 262-281: two componentInstance blocks with no <identifier>, against check_lightning_record_page_configuration.py:256-262 'no <identifier>; required from API 53.0'. M3-S05 caught it and added them; the sample should be fixed at source so the next plan does not have to.

process_observations.observation: A step's inputs.answers[] can list a clarification whose status is open, and nothing in build_plan.py validate flags it — the field's name asserts an answer that does not exist.

evidence.detail: 9 of 16 steps list at least one open question in inputs.answers; validate reports 1 WARN and it is about a checker argument form. Caught only by hand-crossing inputs.answers against clarifications[].status. A validate WARN on the cross-reference would have caught PV-B04 and PV-B05 at plan time.

process_observations.observation: Two of the five blockers are refutations on the conservative side: the missing xml and manifest declarations on M2-S04 and M3-S04 have low practical impact because section 5 runs both checks always-on whether declared or not.

evidence.detail: section 5 'it runs what the plan declares plus the always-on xml and manifest checks' — against the testability lens row that refutes a metadata step carrying neither. The contract couples a fired row to a refuted lens and a refuted lens to a blocker, so both were recorded as blockers with the low impact stated in the blocker text rather than demoted.

process_observations.observation: M4-S01 is a custom-type step owned by metadata-builder that emits no metadata at all, only a deploy-order note, so the agent-covers-the-job check rests on a single Output Contract deliverable.

evidence.detail: Output Contract deliverable 7 names the deploy-order note and the build-scoped outputs name deploy-order.md, so the step is legal under section 4's custom row; but the agent's What This Agent Does is written entirely around emitting -meta.xml files.

process_observations.observation: The plan should return to the planner: five blockers across five steps, two of which are one-line test additions and three of which need a decision or an assumptions row.

evidence.detail: status is now plan-rejected; version stays 1 and the v1 body is archived in history[]; the planner's next set-plan becomes v2.

process_observations.followup_reason: The verifier refutes; the planner repairs. All five blockers are plan edits, not artefact edits.

followups.because: Five blockers are plan-side edits — a decision to re-ground, four assumptions rows to add, and two acceptance_tests entries to declare.
Two blockers and two of the three concerning observations cluster on one architectural decision, whether the approval process ships active.
